pages.text: Near a quiet pond, Freddy hears tiny plops. Spring is here, and the pond feels like a nursery.
Jelly-like frog eggs float gently. Frogs lay eggs in water so babies can grow safely at first.
Days pass, and tadpoles hatch! They look like little commas with tails, wiggling through the pond.
Tadpoles breathe with gills, like fish. They stay in water while their bodies change slowly.
One tadpole grows back legs, then front legs. The tail shrinks as the frog body forms.
Freddy’s skin stays moist and smooth. Amphibians need damp skin, so they like wet places.
Now a young frog pops onto land. Frogs can live near water and hop onto shore to explore.
Freddy catches bugs with a quick tongue flick. Insect snacks help frogs grow strong.
At sunset, Freddy returns to the pond edge. Water is still important for resting and staying moist.
Bedtime lesson: eggs become tadpoles, tadpoles become frogs. Growing and changing is called metamorphosis!
